cards.headline: National Day deals at Mandai Wildlife Reserve; Aug 9 fun at National Museum of S'pore; Mandarin play The Forest Heroes
bullets: Mandai Wildlife Reserve offers up to 30 per cent off admission until Aug 31.
National Museum of Singapore has free activities on Aug 9, including storytelling and a colouring contest.
The National Day Parade will be broadcast live on big screens at Mandai Wildlife Reserve and the National Museum.
Mandarin play 'The Forest Heroes' explores friendship and nature for kids aged five and up from Sept 11.

cards.headline: This Normal stream student thought he was a failure. Now he’s opening doors for students like him
bullets: Clarence Ching started a charity called Access Singapore to help students from poor backgrounds get more chances in life.
He felt like a failure in school because he was in the Normal stream and struggled with ADHD.
Ching believes connections and mentors are as important as good grades for students.
He worked for a Member of Parliament and gained confidence through helping others.
He started his charity after realising many students lack social connections and confidence.

cards.headline: Young S’poreans see promise in job tasters, but hope for deeper and more targeted career support
bullets: Over 10,000 job taster spots will be available in 2026 under the new SG Youth Plan.
The plan offers young people job tasters, mentoring, and adulting programmes.
Job tasters give youth a first look at different workplaces and industries.
Some young people find the new career support reassuring amid job worries.
Others feel more support is needed for those already in the workforce.

cards.headline: Condo VIP sales need clearer rules and limits to ensure transparency
bullets: Agents bought 20% of units at Emerald of Katong before public sales.
Some buyers cancelled deals, losing money, to get VIP sale units.
Concerns raised that regular buyers are disadvantaged by early sales.
Property agents bought 4.2% of new private homes via priority queues.
Regulators are discussing clearer rules for VIP condo sales.

cards.headline: More young S’poreans under 35 want to live independently. Will a new co-living initiative help?
bullets: Over 22,600 young Singaporeans under 35 lived alone in 2025, more than double the 2016 number.
A new co-living scheme offers over 100 subsidised rental units for those aged 21 to 35.
Young people are seeking independence and privacy, leading them to move out earlier.
Co-living spaces aim to provide flexible leases and shared facilities for younger adults.
High rental costs, starting at $1,800, may still be a challenge for some.

cards.headline: Man arrested after marble fired from catapult allegedly damages Woodlands flat window
bullets: A 56-year-old man was arrested for shooting marbles with a catapult at birds.
One marble allegedly hit and damaged a flat window in Woodlands.
Police seized a catapult, marbles, and pebbles from the man.
He will be charged with committing a rash act.

cards.headline: Missing Singaporean woman found in Cambodia says she was not forced into scam activities
bullets: Missing Singaporean Aishah Siregar found safe in Cambodia.
She says she went to Cambodia to teach English, not for scams.
Aishah left Singapore because life felt stressful, she stated.
She deliberately cut contact with family after arriving in Cambodia.

cards.headline: More students can pursue mother tongue languages under expanded programme from 2027
bullets: More students can study Tamil and Chinese languages at a higher level from 2027.
The Malay language special programme will also be expanded to more students.
Tamil language studies will be offered at more schools through a central centre.
A new AI tool will help mark Chinese essays in secondary schools from September.

cards.headline: TikTok CEO Chew Shou Zi urges NTU doctoral graduates to 'actively seek the unknown' at conferment ceremony
bullets: TikTok boss Chew Shou Zi told NTU PhD graduates to seek the unknown.
He spoke about his journey from Yio Chu Kang to leading the social media giant.
Chew urged graduates to use their skills to solve real-world problems.
He encouraged them to embrace uncertainty for innovation.
NTU's 2026 convocation is its largest ever with over 14,000 graduates.

cards.headline: Singapore deepens Latin America ties as MERCOSUR trade pact takes effect for Brazil
bullets: Singapore's trade deal with South American bloc MERCOSUR is now active for Brazil.
This pact aims to cut trade barriers and boost business between Singapore and four Latin American countries.
Brazil is MERCOSUR's biggest economy and a key trading partner for Singapore in the region.
The deal could help Singapore businesses access new markets and diversify food sources.

cards.headline: Fifa’s Infantino faces crisis as Uefa, Concacaf declare no confidence in him over scrapped World Cup deal
bullets: Fifa president Gianni Infantino faces a crisis after Uefa and Concacaf lost confidence in him.
This follows his scrapped plan to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights.
European football body Uefa called the move a victory for the game.
Concacaf said Infantino's actions showed leadership that stopped putting football first.
The backlash may hurt his chances of re-election in 2027.

cards.headline: Spider-Man: Brand New Day heads for US$875 million global opening, defying superhero slump
bullets: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is set to make US$875 million globally on its opening weekend.
The movie is expected to earn US$325 million in North America alone.
This opening is one of the biggest ever, close behind Avengers: Endgame.
Critics and audiences have praised the film, with a 98% positive Rotten Tomatoes score.
The movie resonated with younger audiences, particularly Gen Z.

cards.headline: New Zealand housing market faces biggest ‘down phase’ in decades
bullets: New Zealand house prices hit a three-year low in July.
This is the weakest housing market there in decades.
Prices are still 18 per cent down from their peak in early 2022.
High interest rates and global worries are making buyers hesitant.
A recovery in prices is not expected anytime soon.

cards.headline: A Silicon Valley enclave topples Miami island as the most expensive US ZIP code
bullets: Atherton, a town in Silicon Valley, is now the most expensive US ZIP code.
Five houses there sold for over US$30 million this year, with more expected.
The median home price jumped 20 per cent to nearly US$10 million.
Tech riches from AI and IPOs are driving up demand for luxury homes.

cards.headline: Porsche Macan GTS Electric review: The three-letter code only Porsche people understand
bullets: The new electric Porsche Macan GTS costs S$365,988 without COE.
It has 563 horsepower and can go from 0 to 100 kmh in 3.8 seconds.
The car offers a range of 513 km and charges to 80% in 21 minutes.
It features a synthetic engine sound and a well-connected driving feel.
The electric Macan has improved rear legroom and a 476-litre boot.

cards.headline: S'pore man, 21, arrested for allegedly brandishing 40cm knife during Selegie Road dispute
bullets: A 21-year-old man was arrested for allegedly showing a 40cm knife during a fight on Selegie Road.
The man hid the knife before confronting three other people early Saturday morning.
Police found the knife later along Middle Road.
He faces charges for carrying a weapon in public.

cards.headline: S'porean reported missing in Vietnam arrested over alleged link to etomidate vape syndicate
bullets: A Singaporean man reported missing in Vietnam was arrested for allegedly supplying drugs for a vape syndicate.
He is accused of providing etomidate-laced e-liquid to the group.
Vietnamese police arrested 65 people, including four Singaporeans, in connection with the syndicate.
Two men, one Malaysian and one Singaporean, are believed to be the ringleaders.
Police seized over 1,300 vape cartridges and drug-laced liquid.

cards.headline: S'pore policeman, 47, loses appeal & gets longer jail term for abetting fatal abuse of Myanmar helper
bullets: A police officer's jail term for his role in a maid's death has been increased to over 11 years.
He was found guilty of helping his wife abuse the Myanmar domestic helper.
The officer also tried to hide evidence and lied to police.
His wife is serving 30 years, and her mother 17 years, for the abuse.
The maid died after months of abuse and starvation.

cards.headline: First Look At Aperia Mall’s Refreshed Spaces – New F&B Wing, Playground, & Upgraded Amenities
bullets: Aperia Mall has a new food wing with popular chains like Wang Fu Dim Sum and Subway.
A new playground is now open on the rooftop for kids.
The mall features new murals by local artist Nuriman.
New sheltered pick-up and drop-off points make getting to the mall easier.
Enjoy free parking, bouncy castles, and food deals until September.

cards.headline: We Checked Out Trifecta At Somerset’s New Finnish Sauna, Sheltered Pickleball Court & Vinyl Lounge
bullets: Somerset's TRIFECTA now has a sheltered pickleball court, Finnish sauna, and vinyl lounge.
You can rent the pickleball court for $70.85 per hour, with paddles and balls included.
The new sauna and ice bath area offers contrast therapy for relaxation.
TRIFECTA's Riders' Lounge features food from Yeast Side and a vinyl bar.
A free outdoor gym for functional training will open by the end of the year.

cards.headline: How To Earn Rewards Like Cash By Reading 15 Minutes A Day With NLB’s New ReadSG Movement
bullets: The National Library Board is starting a new movement called ReadSG to encourage reading for 15 minutes daily.
Participants can earn rewards like cash by logging their reading sessions on the CrowdTaskSG platform.
A related initiative, Read for Good, lets people raise funds for charities by reading daily.
NLB aims to get 150,000 people to sign up for these reading programmes.
